subject: How can I switch between versions of brms?

messages.author: 996c974b91f061b6
messages.subject: How can I switch between versions of brms?
parts:
I accidentally installed 1.5.0 without knowing, and realised that I can't plot my models that I ran using 1.4.0.
Am an R/github/model newbie and was wondering if anyone can help? 

Currently using this code to install the latest version of brms. 

install.packages("devtools")

install_github("paul-buerkner/brms", dependencies=TRUE)


Would appreciate it any advice for a code to get the previous version back (so I can switch between versions). 

Thank you! Vivian

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: How can I switch between versions of brms?
parts:
What is it that does not work with brms 1.5.0 anymore? This should not happen. brms 1.5.0 should be fully compatible with models fitted with 1.4.0 and if not I will fix that.

In the meantime, you can install brms 1.4.0 via

packageurl <- "http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/brms/brms_1.4.0.tar.gz"
install.packages(packageurl, repos=NULL, type="source")

Best,
Paul

Hello Paul,

Thanks so much for the quick response.

I ran many models in 1.4.0 (and also previous versions I too) and saved them as an Rdata file.
When I reload the rdata file (either typing nM1 or summary(nM1)), I get this error message. 

nM1 <- brm(Coral~ NCS + s(Year, by=NCS) + s(COTSz, by=NCS, k=4) + s(Wind_Stress, by=NCS, k=4) + s(DHW, by=NCS, k=4) + s(Plume_Freq, by=NCS, k=4) + t2(Lon,Lat) + (1|Reef) + (1|YEAR),

data=LTMP,

family=Beta(),

prior=prior,

control=list(adapt_delta=0.99),

warmup=2000,iter=12000,chains=5,cores=12)


nM1
summary(nM1)

Error in `rownames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("b_Intercept", "b_NCScentral",  : 
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

Another message I have seen when I tried rerunning my codes is this, but I can't seem to replicate it now is this (that's why I figured it was the difference in versions): Error: invalid version specification ‘list(c(1, 5, 0))’, ‘list(c(2, 14, 1))’

Also, is it possible to see the errors on the model apart from when it gets spit out in the console? 

E.g. divergent transitions after warmup?

Thanks for your help, Vivian

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: How can I switch between versions of brms?
parts:
This is definitely something that should not happen and likely affects other users as well.

I was able to trace it back and fix in on github so that the latest dev version should work again without problems.

Alternatively, you can use summary(nM1, use_cache = FALSE) for your models.

Could you also inform me once (and where) you see ‘list(c(1, 5, 0))’, ‘list(c(2, 14, 1))’ again?

Thank you very much for your help!

messages.subject: Re: How can I switch between versions of brms?
parts:
Dear Paul,

Thank you so much for your quick help! Will let you know when I can find the other error code again.

There's one other important question that I have:

Is it possible to run the same code twice (with same data), just on different R sessions and get a different WAIC/LOO but exactly the same summary estimates? It's not a small difference but a big one. e.g. WAIC from -2800 became 11504. I did this last night because I thought I won't be able to retrieve my old models and did a rerun of the same model (thanks for fixing it).

And when I tried to plot the posterior predictive checks, the model went from a very nice fit to a very bad fit, and I can't quite figure out what the difference was. I can't even reproduce the nice plots because even when I used the old Rdata file, it gives me the newer plot. One possible reason is that I plotted it wrong, but I just used the following code: 

pp_check(nM14, nsamples=10000). 

Today I tried two ways, the above and below, but both yielded the same results (bad plot). 

pp_check(y,yrep_nM14[1:10000,], ppc_dens_overlay) 

Any expert thoughts from you is much appreciated. Unfortunately, this model takes overnight to run. I'm running a 3rd one to see if the results are the same. Perhaps the only way is to try and install the old version (10.4.0) to see if I can get the old PPC plots? 

Many thanks, Vivian

This is definitely something that should not happen and likely affects other users as well.

Alternatively, you can use summary(nM1, use_cache = FALSE) for your models.

Could you also inform me once (and where) you see ‘list(c(1, 5, 0))’, ‘list(c(2, 14, 1))’ again?

Thank you very much for your help!
